rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the eight-peak elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing retained compounds. The moderate temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.

Double the gradient time while holding composition and temperature fixed to test which clustered pairs respond to slope. All peaks eluted early in the scouting run, so this should improve diagnostic separation without approaching the acquisition limit.
Keep the improved gradient slope and raise temperature to shift selectivity at the remaining unresolved pair. This also provides additional margin below the 10-minute time-penalty threshold.

The temperature change strongly shifted selectivity but introduced new co-elutions, so test the cooler end of the range at the same slope. This may separate the central cluster while keeping the final peak near the 10-minute threshold.

Raise the starting organic fraction while preserving nearly the same gradient slope as injection 4 to bring the final peak below 10 minutes. This tests whether trimming the weak-solvent segment also improves the marginal central pair without losing the favorable low-temperature selectivity.

Slightly steepen the best gradient while retaining the favorable 25 C selectivity. The marginal central pair worsened slightly with the shallower slope in injection 5, so this tests the opposite direction and further shortens retention.

The controlled slope comparison shows that a shallower gradient improves the remaining critical pair. Combine a shallower slope with a higher starting organic fraction to recover that resolution while targeting a last peak below 10 minutes.

Injection 7 reached the maximum CRF, so now test a shorter fully resolved method. Shift the starting composition upward while preserving its gradient slope, aiming to shorten retention without losing resolution.

Lengthen injection 8’s gradient by one grid step to recover resolution at its sole deficient pair. Its 1.63-minute margin below the time threshold allows a shallower slope while potentially retaining a shorter separation than injection 7.

Test a single temperature step above injection 9 to shorten the fully resolved separation and assess local selectivity changes. Injection 9 remains the shorter maximum-score fallback if warming compromises a neighboring pair.

Test the upper temperature limit using the established scouting slope: the 40–50 C results suggest that further temperature shifts may separate the pairs crossing near 50 C. The low starting organic fraction protects retention of the earliest peak while exploring a faster maximum-score alternative.

Make the high-temperature gradient one step shallower to test whether its sole under-resolved pair reaches baseline resolution. The last peak at 8.56 minutes leaves room for this adjustment without incurring a time penalty.

The shallower high-temperature gradient worsened the critical pair, so test one step steeper than injection 11. This should improve that pair and shorten the run, while checking whether the central pair retains sufficient resolution.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving injection 13’s slope to test a small selectivity adjustment at its marginal central pair. This should also shorten retention, with injection 9 retained as the fully resolved fallback.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 14 to improve both central pairs while retaining its favorable late-pair separation. The trimmed endpoint remains well above the observed elution window, targeting full resolution in roughly seven to eight minutes.

Fine-tune the slope from 0.04583 to 0.045 organic fraction per minute to lift the marginal central pairs above 1.5 while preserving the late pair’s remaining margin. The endpoint remains above the last peak’s estimated elution composition.

Test a higher starting organic fraction to shorten retention, with a shallower slope to help offset compression of the central cluster. Injection 16 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method if this adjustment loses resolution.

Make injection 17’s slope shallower to improve its only deficient pair, while checking the opposing response of the later critical pair. This tests whether the higher starting composition can support full resolution near the retention time of injection 16.

Return to the favorable low-temperature selectivity and test a narrower, shallower gradient with a higher starting composition. This explores a shorter fully resolved alternative to injection 9 while retaining injection 16 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test beyond the apparent pair crossings near 30 C using injection 9’s gradient. A further temperature step may restore separation after elution-order changes while shortening retention toward the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test another temperature beyond the central-cluster crossings to look for a faster fully resolved selectivity window. Injection 16 already secures the maximum CRF, so this remaining exploration targets shorter retention rather than a higher possible score.

Test the remaining high-temperature selectivity window at the same gradient as injection 21. This may separate pairs after their temperature-dependent crossings and yield a shorter maximum-score method; injection 16 remains the confirmed fallback.

Warm the fully resolved method from injection 19 by one step to shorten retention. Its larger separation in the early cluster may tolerate the temperature shift that limited injection 10, while injection 16 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test the intermediate temperature between injections 20 and 21, where the central pair may have separated after changing elution order and the late pair may retain more resolution than at 45 C. This targets a faster fully resolved alternative while preserving injection 16 as the confirmed maximum-score fallback.

Test one step steeper than injection 23 to shorten retention and potentially improve its sole deficient late pair, while checking the marginal central pairs. The maximum CRF is already secured; injection 16 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method if this final refinement fails.
